sources.label: W3C - Web Cryptography API (base SubtleCrypto interface the draft extends)

inputs.rationale: sharedKey and ciphertext are dictionary fields, not callables: the page's Syntax IDL declares them with no parameter list (CryptoKey sharedKey / ArrayBuffer sharedKey / ArrayBuffer ciphertext inside dictionary EncapsulatedKey/EncapsulatedBits), so there is no input contract to state.

errors.rationale: A dictionary field raises nothing: the draft's section 4 carries no field-level error prose, and the named throws and normalization rejections belong to the six methods (sections 3.2.1 through 3.2.5), which are documented on their own rows.

context.rationale: The two dictionaries declare no [SecureContext] or Exposed attribute in the page's Syntax IDL, and the interface-level [SecureContext, Exposed=(Window,Worker)] marker sits on the partial interface SubtleCrypto (section 3), not on these fields, so no context restriction attaches to them.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The WICG draft has no dedicated Security/Privacy Considerations section, so it is silent on field-level security/privacy; the only statements are the section 4 definition sentences, which the page's field table records - the absence is the answer, not a fabricated fact.

notes: SEVEN inventory rows, not eight: the six SubtleCrypto methods (encapsulateKey, encapsulateBits, decapsulateKey, decapsulateBits, getPublicKey, static supports) plus ONE folded row named 'Encapsulation dictionary fields (sharedKey, ciphertext)' covering the two dictionary fields. The fold is deliberate (rule 73): sharedKey and ciphertext are the two members of the EncapsulatedKey and EncapsulatedBits dictionaries, and their only real difference is a type declaration (CryptoKey vs ArrayBuffer sharedKey; ArrayBuffer ciphertext in both), which lives in the IDL - so a single row that names BOTH members is the truthful description, and the declared-surface check still accounts for both names because the folded row's name carries the sharedKey and ciphertext tokens. The two fields are NOT SubtleCrypto members: the page's own 'six new SubtleCrypto members' phrasing counts only the six methods, so 'six SubtleCrypto members' and 'seven inventory rows (eight declared IDL member names)' are both true and count different scopes. outOfScope is empty because all eight declared members are accounted for (six by their own rows, two by the folded row). The JsonWebKey extension is described in prose and deliberately NOT reproduced as IDL: the WICG source DOES contain a 'partial dictionary JsonWebKey { DOMString pub; DOMString priv; }' block (section 5, #x5-partial-jsonwebkey-dictionary), but the page reproduces it only as a prose sentence, so pub/priv are in the source but not in the page's declared IDL surface, and are therefore not a 9th/10th member and not additional field rows - a later reader must not read the seven-row inventory as having missed that block. The page's IDL is copied verbatim from the WICG draft: the six methods from WICG section 3 (#partial-subtlecrypto-interface) and the two dictionaries from WICG section 4 (#x4-encapsulation-dictionaries). The page also declares enum extensions (KeyFormat adds raw-public/raw-private/raw-seed/raw-secret; KeyUsage adds encapsulateKey/encapsulateBits/decapsulateKey/decapsulateBits) - these are enum value additions, not SubtleCrypto or dictionary members, so they are outside the measured roster and are not inventory rows or out-of-scope entries. ERRORS DIMENSION: the page's new Errors section (#errors) documents the six methods' failure sites as two distinct kinds - twelve named DOMException throw sites (catchable by name) and six unnamed promise rejections produced by algorithm normalization (whose value is the normalization result itself, carrying no name to catch) - plus supports()'s no-throw contract and the one implied WebIDL binding-level TypeError from the [EnforceRange] length parameter, which is not an algorithm step. Every throw/rejection site is attributed to the WICG draft section 3.2; the W3C Web Cryptography API base Recommendation is named only to state it contributes none of these sites. LIFECYCLE: the page's new Lifecycle section (#lifecycle) records, per method, whether the draft states the promise/parallel-task pattern - the five asynchronous methods state it (the four quoted sentences plus the throw-to-rejection convention), and supports() does not (synchronous, no promise), which the page records as an absence the source itself makes. EXAMPLES: the page's Examples section (#examples) documents the six methods - the existing composed ML-KEM encapsulate/decapsulate snippet plus a new composed snippet covering encapsulateBits/decapsulateBits/getPublicKey; the WICG draft provides no JavaScript example (the page's own citation says so), so the examples are page-composed from the WICG interface and ML-KEM registered names, and the composed-prose honesty label is carried rather than a source quote. DICTIONARY FIELD CELLS: the folded row's inputs, errors, context and securityPrivacy are not-applicable with page-local reasons (a dictionary field declares no parameter list in the page's IDL; a field raises nothing, the throw/reject sites belong to the six methods; the two dictionaries carry no [SecureContext]/Exposed attribute so the interface-level marker does not attach to them; and the WICG draft has no dedicated Security/Privacy Considerations section, so the draft is silent on field-level security/privacy - the absence is the answer, not a fabricated fact). The field's outputs is documented from the algorithm-setting sentence (section 3.2.1 'Let encapsulatedKey be a new EncapsulatedKey dictionary with sharedKey set to sharedKey and ciphertext set to the ciphertext field of encapsulatedBits'), not from the type-only IDL. The field's compatibility is documented against the page's own field-table compatibility row, which records the absence - BCD api/SubtleCrypto.json carries no sharedKey and no ciphertext key (only the six method keys), so the field's compatibility datum is 'no BCD entry'. COMPATIBILITY SOURCING: the six methods' compatibility cells are sourced from BCD api/SubtleCrypto.json; the static supports() BCD key is literally supports_static (there is no top-level supports key), which the page's citation records. ChromeStatus and the Chromium runtime flag are cited by the page for ship-state provenance but are not used as evidence for any documented compatibility cell because the compatibility table itself is BCD; the three-way shipped-state disagreement (ChromeStatus 'Proposed' with no desktop milestone vs BCD Chrome 155 experimental vs Chromium trunk runtime flag 'stable') is recorded, not resolved, on the page and is attributed to its documents. All selector fragments (#syntax, #errors, #lifecycle, #examples, #browser-compatibility) point at the page's section ids, which are added in the same change as this contract.
